$comment: Hammer-test catalogue: real public repos at real commits. Every SHA was shallow-fetched by SHA from github.com on 2026-10-06 and every listed lockfile line was read at that commit (raw.githubusercontent.com and git show). Nothing here is a fixture. expect[].level is a MINIMUM: 'critical' = must be critical; '>=high' = high or critical; 'present' = a finding row for the purl must exist (any level); 'none' = the purl must NOT appear as a finding. expectAbsent entries are 'level:<lvl>' (no finding at that level), 'reason:<kind>' (no finding carrying that reason) or a purl. sources = external hosts the scenario's assertions depend on; when a host is blocked the dependent assertions are reported as 'blocked: <host>'.

scenarios.why: event-stream 3.3.6 -> flatmap-stream 0.1.1 (Nov 2018) as a RUNTIME (non-dev) dependency in a real lockfile v1; replay after public disclosure.

expect.note: KB INC-2018-0001; npm replaced the package with a security holder, so registry enrichment may be partial

scenarios.verified: git fetch --depth=1 of the SHA succeeded (commit 2018-10-08T14:02:54-05:00). package-lock.json (lockfileVersion 1, 346 entries): line 603 "event-stream": { line 604 "version": "3.3.6" (no dev flag); line 743 "flatmap-stream": { line 744 "version": "0.1.1". Tree has 1 package-lock.json, no workflows.

scenarios.why: Same 2018 incident in an org repo where it is a DEV dependency, scanned at today's date (no replay): malware must not be down-weighted to non-critical just because it is dev-scoped, and the advisory path (OSV) must work without time travel.
scenarios.verified: git fetch --depth=1 of the SHA succeeded (commit 2019-07-29T10:08:19-07:00, current HEAD of the repo). package-lock.json (lockfileVersion 1, 305 entries): line 682 "event-stream": { line 683 "version": "3.3.6"; line 810 "flatmap-stream": { line 811 "version": "0.1.1"; both dev: true.

scenarios.why: ua-parser-js 0.7.29 (Oct 22 2021 account takeover) resolved in a real lockfile committed during the incident window; the next commit c8f50c4f (dependabot 'Bump ua-parser-js from 0.7.29 to 0.7.30') is the fix.

expect.note: KB INC-2021-0001; GHSA-pjwm-rvh2-c87w; npm removed 0.7.29 so the packument lacks it

scenarios.verified: git fetch --depth=2 of fix commit c8f50c4f1acaa93c48815620f38ffc7516bdbbc8 gave parent 86c582c0 (2021-10-22T16:48:52+02:00); the fix commit touches only package-lock.json. At 86c582c0, package-lock.json (lockfileVersion 1, 1330 entries): line 10992 "ua-parser-js": { line 10993 "version": "0.7.29" (dev: true).

scenarios.why: node-ipc 9.2.2 + peacenotwar 9.1.6 (Mar 2022 protestware) via @vue/cli-shared-utils 4.5.15; the next commit d1a93658 'update @vue/cli to mitigate peacenotwar event' is the fix. KB INC-2022-0002 lists only node-ipc 10.1.1/10.1.2, so this probes a real KB coverage gap: a finding must exist, but it is not expected to be critical from the KB alone.

expect.note: INC-2022-0003 lists 9.2.2 (pulls in peacenotwar). It came out low before that KB entry existed; anything below critical is a regression.
protestware payload package, covered by INC-2022-0003.

scenarios.verified: git fetch --depth=2 of fix commit d1a93658fa12956a8a0bb8d16ff185421e653dfe gave parent 6842cfb6 (2022-03-19T13:20:46+11:00); the fix touches package-lock.json. At 6842cfb6, package-lock.json (lockfileVersion 2, 1100 entries): line 6886 "node_modules/node-ipc": { line 6887 "version": "9.2.2" (dev: true); line 7645 "node_modules/peacenotwar": { line 7646 "version": "9.1.6". colors resolves to 1.4.0 (not affected). No compromised node-ipc 10.1.1/10.1.2 lockfile could be found on GitHub code search.

scenarios.why: colors 1.4.2 (Jan 2022 sabotage) committed into a real org repo lockfile on 2022-01-10, inside the incident window; still the repo HEAD today.
scenarios.verified: git fetch --depth=1 of the SHA succeeded (commit 2022-01-10T18:35:17+01:00, current HEAD). package-lock.json (lockfileVersion 1): line 773 "colors": { line 774 "version": "1.4.2", resolved https://registry.npmjs.org/colors/-/colors-1.4.2.tgz, dev: true. Second lockfile benchmark/package-lock.json has no KB hit. Registry time: colors 1.4.2 published 2022-01-09T19:35:35Z.

scenarios.why: faker 6.6.6 (Jan 2022 sabotage) still pinned TODAY at HEAD of a well-known org's repo: a current, not historical, blast radius.
scenarios.verified: git fetch --depth=1 of the SHA succeeded (commit 2025-11-05T02:41:01+06:00, current HEAD). package-lock.json (lockfileVersion 3, 302 entries): line 1904 "node_modules/faker": { line 1905 "version": "6.6.6" (dev: true).

scenarios.why: Outbound/CI blast radius: Renovate merged 'update tj-actions/changed-files digest to 0e58ed8' on 2025-03-14T22:54Z, pinning the workflow to the exact compromised commit (it was reverted the next day by 745b8990). Every other action in the repo is SHA-pinned, so this is the only expected critical. The commit 0e58ed86 itself is no longer fetchable from tj-actions (not our ref), so the engine must not need to fetch it.

expect.note: KB INC-2025-0001 (severity high, ci_compromise); used in .github/workflows/linters.yml

scenarios.verified: git fetch --depth=1 of the SHA succeeded (merge commit 2025-03-14T22:54:08Z). git grep at that commit: .github/workflows/linters.yml:24 '- uses: tj-actions/changed-files@0e58ed8671d6b60d0890c21b07f8835ace038e67 # v45'. 11 workflow files; no package-lock.json. Sibling repo torana-us/terraform-modules@69e65ed12de7b4a6ad386fd280cab04b5867b866 has the same line (spare).

scenarios.why: Sep 8 2025 chalk/debug phishing compromise: lockfile committed on the incident day (2025-09-08T17:14+01:00) resolving six compromised versions at once. All of these versions were later unpublished from npm, so registry lookups for them must degrade gracefully.
scenarios.verified: git fetch --depth=1 of the SHA succeeded (commit 2025-09-08T17:14:00+01:00, current HEAD). package-lock.json (lockfileVersion 3, 419 entries): line 4142 node_modules/ora/node_modules/chalk 5.6.1; line 1726 node_modules/debug 4.4.2; line 5743 node_modules/wrap-ansi/node_modules/ansi-styles 6.2.2; line 5168 node_modules/strip-ansi 7.1.1; line 1190 node_modules/ansi-regex 6.2.1; line 1853 node_modules/error-ex 1.3.3 (all dev: true).

scenarios.why: Healthy control: well-maintained repo at a recent commit, one lockfile (242 entries) and 13 workflows. No KB-listed version present.
scenarios.verified: git fetch --depth=1 of the SHA succeeded (commit 2026-10-06T16:38:13Z). Only package-lock.json in tree (lockfileVersion 3, 242 entries). Swept every entry against all npm purls/versions in kb/incidents: 0 hits.

scenarios.why: Healthy control with 3 lockfiles (root, docs/, repro/) and 15 workflows: exercises multi-asset grouping without any expected critical.
scenarios.verified: git fetch --depth=1 of the SHA succeeded (commit 2026-10-02T21:35:45-04:00). Lockfiles: package-lock.json (742 entries), docs/package-lock.json (619), repro/package-lock.json (8). KB sweep: 0 hits.

scenarios.why: Scale: one very large real lockfile (3353 install entries, 2793 unique name@version, 1.7 MB) plus 3 more lockfiles and 56 workflows in the full repo. Stresses ingest, enrichment batching and the findings table.
scenarios.verified: git fetch --depth=1 of the SHA succeeded (commit 2026-10-06T16:48:40-04:00). Lockfiles: superset-frontend/package-lock.json (lockfileVersion 3, 3353 entries), superset-embedded-sdk (345), superset-websocket (221), superset-websocket/utils/client-ws-app (133) = 4052 entries; plus 1 yarn/pnpm lockfile (unsupported). KB sweep: 0 hits. Advisory (vuln) findings are allowed.

scenarios.why: Scale: 65 package-lock.json files (61 outside node_modules paths) with 6200 install entries / 3048 unique components across many assets, plus 19 workflows. Target for the 5k+ row UI stress (component x asset rows) and graph rendering.
scenarios.verified: git fetch --depth=1 --filter=blob:none of the SHA succeeded (commit 2026-10-07T00:27:25+02:00). ls-tree: 65 package-lock.json, 0 yarn/pnpm, 19 workflows. Read all 61 non-node_modules lockfiles via git show: 6200 entries, 3048 unique name@version; KB sweep 0 hits.

scenarios.why: Robustness + scale on a real repo full of deliberately odd lockfiles: 97 package-lock/shrinkwrap files (7587 parseable entries), 3 of which are not valid JSON (merge-conflict markers in workspaces/arborist/test/fixtures/conflict-package-lock, workspace3 fixtures), ancient/invalid lockfile fixtures, and 5 yarn.lock fixtures. The scan must finish, report the unparseable and unsupported lockfiles as warnings and never crash or hang.
scenarios.verified: git fetch --depth=1 --filter=blob:none of the SHA succeeded (commit 2026-10-01T14:02:10-07:00). ls-tree: 97 package-lock.json/npm-shrinkwrap.json, 5 yarn.lock, 26 workflows. JSON.parse fails on workspaces/arborist/test/fixtures/conflict-package-lock/package-lock.json (line 13 '<<<<<<< HEAD') and workspaces/arborist/test/fixtures/workspace3/packages/a/{package-lock.json,npm-shrinkwrap.json}. KB sweep of the rest: 0 hits. Audit fixtures (e.g. audit-all-severities) intentionally contain vulnerable versions, so vuln findings are expected.

scenarios.why: Coverage honesty: the only lockfile is a yarn.lock that resolves ua-parser-js 0.7.29 (fixed by dependabot commit 09036cee). src/ingest/fs.ts classes yarn.lock as unsupportedLockfiles, so the engine cannot see the compromise. The scan and UI must say so loudly (coverage warning naming yarn.lock) instead of showing a clean result.

expect.note: not detectable while yarn.lock is unsupported; the run must surface an 'unsupported lockfile: yarn.lock' coverage warning. If yarn support lands, flip this to critical.

scenarios.verified: git fetch --depth=2 of fix commit 09036ceeae44cd7dd382df47888937e5c37302a2 gave parent 3354bfa6 (2021-10-22T16:56:14+02:00); the fix touches only yarn.lock. At 3354bfa6: yarn.lock line 12207 'ua-parser-js@^0.7.18:' line 12208 'version "0.7.29"'; raw package-lock.json returns 404; ls-tree shows yarn.lock and 2 workflows, no package-lock.json.
